name: Fix it at home
desc: Shutting off water, gas and power, tripped fuses, gas smell, leaks, blocked drains, broken windows

guides.t: Shutting off water, gas and power
guides.w: Find them before you need them
s: Water: the main stopcock is usually near the water meter (in Dutch homes often under the stairs or in the crawl space). Turn it clockwise to close.
Gas: the main valve is next to the gas meter. Handle along the pipe = open; across the pipe = closed.
Power: the main switch is in the fuse box (meter cupboard). Switch it off to make the whole home dead.
Label them, show everyone in the house, and keep a torch next to the fuse box.
Try the water stopcock once a year: old ones get stuck.
d: After closing the gas, let a professional (or the gas company) open it again if you're unsure

guides.t: The power went off in part of the house
guides.w: A switch in the fuse box has flipped
s: Look in the fuse box: one switch (or the earth-leakage switch, often marked with a test button) is down.
Unplug the appliances on that group, or the last thing you switched on.
Switch the group back on. If it's the earth-leakage switch: switch off all groups, put it back up, then switch the groups on one by one.
If it flips again when you switch something on, that appliance is the problem: leave it unplugged.
Flips again with nothing plugged in? Call an electrician.
d: Don't hold a switch up to stop it flipping
Never open the fuse box cover or the meter

guides.w: A rotten-egg smell in the house
s: Don't switch anything on or off: no lights, doorbell, switches or plugs. No flames, no smoking.
Open doors and windows wide.
Close the gas valve at the meter if you can reach it easily.
Get everyone out and warn the neighbours by knocking, not ringing.
Call from outside: in the Netherlands the national outage number 0800-9009; in Italy the gas company's emergency number on your bill, or 112.
Strong smell, or a hissing sound: call 112.
d: Don't use your phone inside the house
Don't go back in until it's been declared safe

s: Close the small valve under the sink or toilet if there is one; otherwise the main stopcock.
Put a bucket under it and towels around it. If water is near sockets or lamps, switch off the power.
A leaking pipe: wrap it tightly with self-amalgamating repair tape or a pipe clamp until a plumber comes.
A dripping tap usually needs a new washer or cartridge: close the water, unscrew the handle and take the old one to the shop.
Photograph any damage for the insurance.
d: Don't touch switches or sockets with wet hands or standing in water

s: Sink: pour a kettle of hot water down slowly (for a toilet use hot tap water, not boiling: it can crack the bowl).
Use a plunger: enough water to cover the cup, cover the overflow hole with a wet cloth, then pump hard 10–15 times.
Sink still blocked: put a bucket under the U-shaped pipe, unscrew it by hand and clean it out.
Toilet: a toilet brush pushed in firmly a few times often helps too.
Still blocked deeper down: call a plumber.
d: Don't keep flushing a blocked toilet: it overflows

s: Wear shoes and thick gloves. Keep children and pets away.
Carefully remove loose pieces, top first, and wrap glass in newspaper or cardboard before throwing it away.
A cracked pane: put strong tape over the cracks in a cross so it doesn't fall out.
Cover the hole with board, cardboard or thick plastic, taped or screwed around the frame.
Take photos for the insurance, then call a glazier.
d: Don't push out a cracked pane with your hand
